subject: Provable control inventory and artefact logistics - SOC2/ISO/SIG follow-up
messages:
From: Brightline Audit - Claire Ng <claire.ng@brightlineaudit.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: HorizonBank - initial control mapping and evidence logistics request

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the call this morning. HorizonBank's audit and procurement teams have asked for a provable control inventory that maps your SOC 2 and ISO 27001 controls to the SIG questionnaire items they sent last week. Specifically they want: 1) a single control index (spreadsheet) enumerating control IDs, control owner, evidence artifacts and locations; 2) an artefact delivery plan that explains how private evidence will be transferred to the auditor (SFTP, Box shuttle, or key-protected Drive link); and 3) a short SLA-exception log for controls that are out-of-scope or under remediation with expected remediation ETA.

Can you confirm whether you can deliver a draft control index and transfer SOP by next Monday (2028-06-04)? Also include any restrictions we should know about (e.g., PII redaction, limited access windows).

Claire Ng
Senior Assurance Manager | Brightline Audit
claire.ng@brightlineaudit.com

Attachments: horizonbank-sig-questions-20280529.pdf (referenced)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Brightline Audit - Claire Ng <claire.ng@brightlineaudit.com>, HorizonBank Procurement <procurement@horizonbank.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonBank - initial control mapping and evidence logistics request

Hi Claire / Horizon procurement team,

Thanks — we can do this. Attached is a first-pass control index (redwood-soc2-control-index-v1.3.xlsx) and a short evidence transfer SOP (evidence-transfer-sop.pdf). The index maps SOC 2 and ISO controls to the SIG sections we examined during the kickoff. It includes a control owner column and an "evidence location" pointer (Drive folder or internal ticket).

Key notes up front:
- We will not deliver raw PII-containing logs; those will be redacted or packaged as hashed extracts per our data minimization policy.
- Evidence transfer options: preferred = secure Drive link with time-limited access; alternate = SFTP for large bundles. See the SOP for steps and expected lead times.
- Controls under remediation are flagged in the index with a short remediation note and an ETA.

Request from your side to make the draft actionable:
1) Confirm the auditor access method preferred (time-limited Drive link vs SFTP).
2) If you require persistent copies inside Horizon's environment, confirm the transfer window and contact for SCP/SFTP credentials.
3) Any SIG sections that need a line-by-line mapping (we flagged high-priority sections in the index).

I'll run a brief internal sprint with Ben and Karthik to fill gaps and prepare the partial SIG answers doc for your review by EOD Monday.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-soc2-control-index-v1.3.xlsx, evidence-transfer-sop.pdf

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: HorizonBank artefact sprint plan (owners + checklist)

Team — quick internal plan before I send the final packet to Claire and procurement. Goal: produce a defensible control index + transfer package by EOD today. Tasks: 
- Karthik: validate control owner names and add system screenshots where we reference runtime isolation (items C-4, I-2 in index).
- Ben: gather and redact logs for the infra access controls; prepare hashed extracts and confirm they conform to the SOP.
- Jasmine: consolidate SIG Qs we can answer now and mark items needing legal review.

Deliverables: control index (v1.4 draft), partial SIG answers doc (sig-questionnaire-partial-answers.docx), zipped transfer bundle (for SFTP option).

If we hit blockers with legal on any answers, escalate to Regina in Legal (I'll loop her if needed).

Thanks — I'll queue the attachments and send the external update after your check-ins.

-Sofia

From: HorizonBank Procurement <procurement@horizonbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Brightline Audit - Claire Ng <claire.ng@brightlineaudit.com>
Date: Wed, 03 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonBank - initial control mapping and evidence logistics request

Hi Sofia,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Horizon prefers time-limited Drive access for initial review (security team will request copies only for items that require deeper forensics). A couple of clarifications from procurement: 
- For any third-party subprocessor attestations referenced in your index, please include the latest policy version and the date of last review.
- We need a short SLA-exception table for any controls where you are requesting an SLA exemption (i.e., transient logs retention shorter than 90 days, 3rd-party-managed encryption key rotations).

If you can include the SLA-exception table in the index and confirm Drive link access policy (who can request extension), we can schedule the Brightline audit team for an initial review on Thursday morning (2028-06-06).

Procurement Analyst — HorizonBank
procurement@horizonbank.com

Note: they attached a bank internal intake form (horizonbank-intake-20280601.pdf) but we haven't received it yet.

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 04 Jun 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: HorizonBank - initial control mapping and evidence logistics request

Claire / Horizon team —

Attached is the updated control index (v1.4 draft) and the partial SIG answers doc. Highlights: 
- SLA-exception table has been added (tab: SLA-Exceptions). Items flagged are mostly retention windows and two encryption key management items; each entry has an owner and remediation ETA.
- Evidence transfer: default workflow = time-limited Drive links (48-hour window). For large bundles (>2GB) we'll provision SFTP and share credentials via encrypted email.
- Subprocessor attestation: we included the policy name and last review date in the control index (column: subprocessor_attestation_date).

Next steps / ask: please confirm Drive access for Brightline auditors (Claire) so I can provision links. If Horizon requires persistent copies or SFTP, let us know the contact for credentials.

Links/attachments: redwood-soc2-control-index-v1.4-draft.xlsx (attached), sig-questionnaire-partial-answers.docx (attached), evidence-transfer-sop.pdf (attached), Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB2cXq-transfer-pack

I'll mark any remaining legal-only items with the tag [LEGAL-REVIEW] in the index and follow up separately.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
